claim: Non-executing CAS findings such as comments, documentation, reports, and commit-message claims are batchable prose work, while behavior defects remain in ordinary fix rounds.

CAS code comments must not cite branch-local plans, specifications, BACKLOG entries, review rounds, finding IDs, or task numbers; when surrounding code already expresses a rule, deleting the comment is preferred.

For `Layout::parseNamespaceFileKey`, a key carrying `/_files/` is only a necessary trigger for namespace-file parsing, not sufficient proof that it is a real namespace file, because `Layout::mountpointObjectKey` does not enforce the `_files` reservation.

`Cas::Gc`'s fold LISTs `casRefsPrefix()` and never `rootsPrefix()`, so `_files` keys do not reach a GC round even though `ContentAddressedTransaction::removeRecursive` handles both the ref-`_log` and `_files` key families.
`RootNamespace` has no constructor taking a `NamespaceLifeId`; the explicitness of its `String` constructor is unrelated to constructibility from `NamespaceLifeId`.
`CommandFsck::executeImpl` does not throw for `stale_edge` in either summary or detail mode, so a detail scan with nonzero `stale_edge` can print a `note:` and still exit with code 0.

`ns_cleanup_items` is keyed by `{ns, remove_txn_id}`, and a namespace can retain multiple `nsc` rows because rows retire only after a later round observes completion artifacts; a ref-folding abort skips retirement.
The `btr` per-run-segment rows and `cnd` per-gc-shard rows are charged neither in `worstCaseEntryFoldReservationBytes`'s fixed term nor in its per-entry term.
`encodeFoldSeal` writes a meta line containing `g`/`pg` between the header and trailer, and `foldSealFixedBytes` is a floor measured at `generation = 0` and `n = 0`, not a constant for every seal.
A persisted `CreatorFence.fence_generation` is not comparable across processes because it is a process-local `std::atomic<uint64_t>` whose counter restarts at zero in another `CasMountRuntime`.
`probeNonTerminalMountSlots` treats an absent mount slot as nothing to hold and an undecodable slot body as held; its conservative precedent applies only to the undecodable-body case.
`CasRefCatalog` has no entry-deletion API in the documented state, so a catalog entry survives unconditionally rather than through a partially completed multi-step removal path.

The ref layer still has read or removal entry points that recover and mint on demand: `CasRefLedger::dropNamespace`, `CasRefLedger::listRefs`, and `CasRefLedger::resolveRef` through `dropRefIfPresent`.
The raw fixture `publishAt` is not the production birth writer: it drains through `writeRefLogTxnRaw`, whose test-only `casAdmitEntry` call admits the namespace into the catalog.
`writeRefSnapshotRaw` does not admit a catalog entry; a caller needing the namespace to be discoverable must call `casAdmitEntry` first, as `writeRefLogTxnRaw` does.
`RefTableRuntime::life` has two writers: `ensureRefTableRecovered` during recovery and step 1 of `namespaceFilesLifeIfReadable`, which can resolve it without recovery.
The runtime size fences drive only the birth-time `_ckpt` writer; fixed-capacity non-heap fields populated by the sealer or snapshot publisher are outside those three fences.
`Pool::listNamespaces` remains LIST-based and was not changed by the catalog-authoritative `Gc::discoverUniverse` switch.
`completeCreation` publishes a namespace `_ckpt` at creation, before any first snapshot publication commits.
In the T1/T6a frontier logic, the `checkpoint_unusable` anomaly bucket represents the no-cursor mechanism; an unreadable `_ckpt` when a cursor exists is reported as `held` instead.
Arithmetic exact-key intake is the intended mechanism for closing LIST omissions; the former Probe A seam was deleted rather than retained as a sampled store-quality detector.
`GcRoundWorkBudget::max_sweep_namespaces` counts cumulatively per round, not per PAGE; the two interpretations coincide only while a sweep takes one page per round.
The user-facing `CasEvent::detail` and fsck-report abbreviations `ns`, `me`, `p`, and `ha` remain an undecided spell-out-versus-keep follow-up.
The grounded `CasListLiarEndToEnd` fixture writes recoverable checkpoints for `hidden` with `committed_through = RefTxnId{1,1}` and `visible` with `committed_through = RefTxnId{1,2}`.

With both namespaces truthfully grounded in the list-liar fixture, `frontier_namespaces = 2 > 0` and `universe_authoritative = true` under `UniversePolicy::kDefault` (`= Authoritative`), so those terms cannot make this fixture's `frontier_complete` false.
The list-liar test's load-bearing property is that `Gc::fold` reads each expected ref-log or checkpoint by exact key, so a LIST omission cannot make a durable edge appear absent.

If `Gc::fold` reads a record only when its key appears in the round's LIST hint, a durable checkpoint-committed ref log omitted by LIST is treated as absent, leaving the namespace held and making the frontier incomplete so destructive work is suppressed.
The `CasGcFrontierGate` exact-key arm finds a hidden edge and saves its blob on a complete frontier; the round is not refused merely because the edge was hidden from LIST.
The retirement-sweep regression test must run 32 rounds because the removed detector enumerated every 16th folding round, and five rounds would not exercise that cadence twice.

The GC log's `phase` column has these 18 execution-order values: `lease`, `pre_fold_ref_drain`, `heartbeat_floor`, `defer_decision`, `parent_seal_read`, `fold_ref_group`, `fold_seal_read`, `fold_ref_intake`, `fold_reduce`, `fold_seal_write`, `pending_deletes`, `meta_pool_wait`, `round_commit`, `handoff_reclaim`, `manifest_deletes`, `namespace_cleanup`, `ref_object_cleanup`, and `orphan_sweep`.
A 30-minute GC round was measured as 3.42 million serial round trips at approximately 0.5 ms each, with phase time attributed to serial request latency rather than CPU or lock time.
Logs for one table must be folded in strict ID order, and a clamp must stop that table at the correct log; prefetching may change only when data is available, never what is applied.
Parallel GC fetching should be bounded by the number of in-flight manifest bodies and should leave application strictly ordered while fetching log and manifest bodies ahead of use.
The measured 959-transaction residual pool contained 7,565 edges over 4,573 distinct manifests, so 39.6% of intake manifest fetches were re-reads; intra-transaction redundancy was exactly zero.
In that fold window, 2,991 manifests carried both an add and a remove edge, and `CasManifestGet == CasRefEmittedEdges`, demonstrating that no manifest-body cache existed.
A proposed manifest cache is keyed by `ManifestId`, scoped to one fold round, bounded in bytes, and dropped at round end; avoiding one redundant edge avoids both its HEAD and GET trips.
The HEAD-before-GET pair remains a protocol step under the standing veto; the proposed cache removes whole redundant edges and therefore does not remove the HEAD from an edge that is still fetched.
A `pending_deletes` occurrence took 77.2 seconds while the next-worst phase took 243 milliseconds, consistent with roughly 150,000 serial `deleteExact` calls at approximately 0.5 ms each.
Each `deleteExact` carries its own token and must remove only the matching object incarnation, preserving GC safety against deletion of a replaced incarnation.

S3 bulk `DeleteObjects` is rejected for `pending_deletes` because it provides no per-object precondition, while `deleteExact` is safety-critical and backends that ignore its condition are rejected by `Cas::Probe`.
A ref-log enumeration returned `0x1430e` while omitting `0x1430c` and `0x1430d`, even though the omitted logs had been durable for nineteen seconds and were written 2.2 ms before the returned log.
The proposed LIST-completeness direction is an authoritative per-namespace CHAIN plus a complete-cut gate: a record whose predecessor link is unaccounted for cannot be passed by a round's seal.
Observed LIST holes are short adjacent runs of 2–15 keys rather than approximately 1000-key pages, so completeness logic must not assume page-shaped holes.
RustFS has demonstrably returned incomplete LIST results, while AWS S3 was untested in the cited investigation; correctness cannot rely on assumed store LIST behavior.

Probe A is the field detector for the observed LIST-omission class, and the HEAD verdict at firing time is needed to distinguish the two opposite defects after the evidence would otherwise be unrecoverable.

The fsck ENTRY gate can safely accept `--partial` for the positive direction: a partial scan that finds `dangling > 0` still fails, while proof of absence must be reported as `unchecked`; the gate currently does not run on a 5.5 GB pool.
`ref_publish` and `ref_drop` audit events currently carry no ref transaction ID, so writer-side append ordering had to be inferred through `blob_storage_log`.
A distinct-manifest counter per GC round would make the manifest re-read ratio continuously observable and test the large-window redundancy prediction.
The fsck detail report found `reachable=17`, `dangling=0`, `unreachable=12`, `pending_gc=0`, `awaiting_gc=0`, `unaccounted=0`, `stale_edge=12`, and `corrupted_runs=0`.

The same fsck report measured `snapshot_oracle_mismatches=0`, `snapshot_oracle_checked=0`, `physical_bytes=21470665670`, `referenced_logical_bytes=75129138898`, `distinct_blobs=17`, `total_blob_refs=54`, and `dedup_ratio=3.17647`.

The fsck report identified 12 unreferenced objects whose only source edges name manifests that no longer exist; their in-degree cannot reach zero, so incremental GC cannot reclaim them and an in-degree rebuild is required to clear the condition.

GC anomaly Probe A recorded durable ref logs `0000000000000001-000000000001430c` and `0000000000000001-000000000001430d` as missing from the pre-fold scan while each had `head='present'`, `pre_max='0000000000000001-000000000001430e'`, `fold_max='0000000000000001-0000000000014a10'`, and `row_cap='32'`.
The GC wedge forensics snapshot for phase-A exit stand seed 991 recorded 63 clamped manifests for namespace `ca_soak_ch1/store/b37/b3781ce3-af83-4732-8c64-e8d342672225@cas@`.
In that wedge snapshot, the first-seen clamp interval was `2026-07-09 22:01:27` through `2026-07-10 02:37:21`, with the recorded value `56826`.
The `disk_transaction_wait_for_blob_removal` server setting defaults to `1` and makes the server wait for background blob removal to complete before acknowledging the operation.
Version 26.3 adds the `DiskObjectStorageWaitBlobRemovalMicroseconds` event for measuring time waiting for object-storage blob removal.
Version 26.3 adds the `SYSTEM WAIT BLOBS CLEANUP` privilege.
